title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models (arXiv record)
note: arXiv record, v1 of 22 Sep 2026 (cs.LG, cs.AI), accepted at ADBIS 2026. Abstract: six pretrained forecasters on energy, traffic and financial data against statistical baselines and one supervised deep model; pretrained models come out ahead, with a trade-off between point accuracy and calibration: xLSTM models stay calibrated across horizons, patch transformers lose calibration at long horizons.

title: Full text: evaluation design
note: Design. Non-overlapping rolling segments of context + 2 horizons; zero-shot models get context plus the first horizon as input, PatchTST trains on it; all are scored on the second. MixGridPL: context 240 h with horizons 12 to 672 h (144 and 288, not 168), or horizon 24 h with contexts 96 to 600 h. Metrics: sMAPE; coverage error (ICE) and interval MAE of the 80% interval. Results are plots only.

title: Full text: MixGridPL accuracy
note: MixGridPL point accuracy in the text. Fixed context: Chronos-2, TiRex and Sundial at sMAPE 3.92 to 3.95% for 12 h, against ARIMA 14% and running average 13%; at 672 h Chronos-2 6.4% and Moirai-2.0 6.6% against ARIMA 19%. At a fixed 24 h horizon Chronos-2 improves from 6.70% to 4.4% as its input grows from 120 to 624 h. No seasonal naive, no regression baseline, no weather input.

title: Full text: calibration
note: Calibration in the text. MixGridPL: TiRex ICE 0.01 to 0.04 in all scenarios; Chronos-2 ICE falls from 0.17 to 0.04 with more context at 24 h; Sundial and PatchTST about 0.45; Moirai ICE 0.01 at 12 h but interval MAE rises from 109 to 479 at long horizons. EdgeTraffic at 1,800 s: TimesFM ICE 0.73, Moirai 0.56, Toto 0.07, Chronos-2 and TiRex under 0.06. No uncertainty interval on any number.

title: GitHub - unic-ailab/TSFM-Eval
note: Authors' repository, Apache-2.0, 21 commits from 11 May to 22 Sep 2026, no tags or releases, 0 stars and forks. Holds forecast_results.parquet (per-step truth, p10/p50/p90, errors, timings) and a notebook that rebuilds plots and aggregates from it. No script that runs the models and no input data were listed. The README gives the paper a different title (adds efficiency). Files not opened.

title: NX-AI/TiRex model card
note: Model card of the central model: TiRex, 35M parameters, xLSTM, univariate zero-shot forecasts with quantiles; default file model.ckpt, plus tirex.onnx. Licence: NXAI community licence. The card points to a newer TiRex-2 with covariates. Installs as tirex-ts, tested on Linux and macOS; custom CUDA kernels are optional.

title: Commit history of model.ckpt, NX-AI/TiRex
note: The weights file model.ckpt has one commit: the repository's first, d76a39c, on 26 May 2025. The API listing of all commits (huggingface.co/api/models/NX-AI/TiRex/commits/main) dates it 2025-05-26 07:15 UTC; later commits are README and licence edits, an ONNX upload on 5 Feb 2026 and a card edit on 13 Nov 2026.

title: LICENSE, NX-AI/TiRex
note: NXAI Community License, modelled on the Llama 3 community licence: free use, modification and redistribution with attribution; an organisation with consolidated annual revenue above EUR 100 million that builds the model into a commercial product or service needs a separate commercial licence. Not Apache-2.0 or MIT.

title: Full text: setup
note: Setup. Six models (Chronos-2, TiRex, Moirai-2.0, Sundial, TimesFM 200M, Toto) at Hugging Face defaults on a T4 GPU, all univariate. Baselines: fixed-order ARIMA, running average, random walk with drift, a small PatchTST. Three single series: EdgeTraffic (1 s counts, 2 h), MixGridPL (Poland grid, hourly, 12,407 points, 2024-25), SPY daily closes. Links the TSFM-Eval repository.

title: search and research: replication or critique of arXiv 2609.25788 (nothing found)
note: One search (title in quotes, replication OR critique OR TSFM-Eval) and one research task at the standard tier found no independent rerun or critique. The search returned the paper itself, a copy on the authors' lab site (linc.ucy.ac.cy, not fetched), an unrelated position paper on benchmark leakage, and a follow-up by two of the same authors. The repository shows 0 stars, 0 forks.

title: research task: which primary sources support or contradict the claims
note: Research answer, 8 sources: the paper, the TiRex card (twice), the repository, the PDF, a later MDPI study, and two Hugging Face listing pages of no use. It points out one xLSTM model cannot stand for a family, Toto is a transformer that stays calibrated, PatchTST is deliberately tiny, and no contamination audit is given. It called the MDPI study external support; that study shares two authors.

title: Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Time Series Models Against Data Degradation in Industrial Sensor Streams (Future Internet 18(10), 550)
note: Later study sharing two authors with the candidate (Michael, Trihinas), so not independent. Chronos, TimesFM and TiRex on sensor streams with gaps and spikes in the context: TiRex intervals stay calibrated, Chronos intervals are over-confident, TimesFM suffers most from long outages. Cites the candidate for the accuracy/calibration trade-off. Only the abstract and introduction were read.
